questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Explain frequency independence to a peer
questions.stem: At fixed amplitude, the intensity ratio for frequencies 3 MHz and 6 MHz is?
questions.explanation: Intensity at fixed amplitude is independent of frequency, so the ratio is 1 regardless of the frequency values.
questions.hint: Frequency does not affect classical intensity.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Detecting a law violation in data
questions.learningObjective: Identify absorption as a cause of faster decay
questions.stem: An astronomer observes intensity decaying faster than inverse-square; which explanation is most plausible?

options.text: Distance has no effect on intensity
The inverse-square law is fundamentally wrong
Absorption by interstellar dust reduces intensity

questions.explanation: Faster-than-inverse-square decay is consistent with absorption by dust or gas. Rejecting the law outright is premature.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute power from intensity at 10 meters
questions.stem: Intensity is 2 watts per square meter at 10 meters; what is the source power?
questions.explanation: Power equals intensity times 4πr², so 2 W/m² times 4π times 100 m² gives about 2513 W. Using πr² or doubling radius changes the area.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute intensity at 6 meters from 36π-watt source
questions.stem: A source radiates 36π watts isotropically; what is the intensity at 6 meters?
questions.explanation: Intensity equals 36π/(4π times 36) = 0.25 W/m². Dropping 4π or mishandling the square gives the wrong values.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Apply E cross B to find propagation direction
questions.stem: If E points west and B points up, which direction does energy propagate?
questions.explanation: West cross up points south, so energy propagates south. Reversing factors or aligning with a field gives the wrong direction.
questions.hint: Apply E cross B with right-hand rule.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute intensity for 50 watts over 0.5 square meters
questions.stem: A detector of area 0.5 square meters receives 50 watts; what is the intensity?
questions.explanation: Intensity equals power per area, so 50 W over 0.5 m² gives 100 W/m². Multiplying or ignoring area gives the wrong values.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.learningObjective: Compute intensity for E0 = 5.0 V/m
questions.stem: For a plane wave with E0 = 5.0 volts per meter, compute the intensity in watts per square meter.
questions.explanation: Using I = (1/2)cε0E0² with E0 = 5.0 V/m gives about 0.0331 W/m². The half factor and constants must both be included.
questions.hint: Use I = c ε0 E0² over 2.
